body: This is sort of a known limitation of our auto-linking feature (which is heuristic-based). As a work-around, you can use `Code here`. Since in this case we can reliably detect that `http://...` does not refer to the `http` package, we should be able to improve our heuristics to exclude such code snippets from matching auto-linking (I've found 11 occurrences of this across all guides and API docs from a quick search). ## If anyone wants to take this on, that would be 👌

issue.body: Previously, our auto-linking feature would match `http` in URLs (such as `http://...`) to the `common/http` package and automatically create a link to that, which was undesirable. While it is possible to work around that via `http://...`, most people didn't even realize the issue. Since in this case it is possible to reliably know it is a false match, this commit fixes it by applying a custom auto-link filter that ignores all docs for `http`, if it comes before `://`. Fixes #31012.
